fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. This one is a daughter, not a son. Luke says Jairus came because “…his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying.” (Luke 8:42) And it's more serious than a fever, since she's dying. Keep that in mind, because the rest of the story leans on it.

You might be thinking of a different story, since Jesus does heal a centurion's paralyzed servant in Matthew 8:5-13. But Jairus is not asking for a servant. The text says he begs Jesus to come because “…his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying.” (Luke 8:42) This one is about a father and his daughter.
Seven is a good Bible number, but it's not the one here. The text says his only daughter "…was about twelve…" (Luke 8:42) So the number we're looking for is twelve, not seven.
Good guess, but she's a little younger than that. Luke says she "…was about twelve…" (Luke 8:42) Notice he says "about," so even the text isn't giving a birthday.

Sacrifices are a fair thought, but Luke doesn't mention them here. He says she "…had spent all her money on physicians…" (Luke 8:43) So her money went to doctors. That's the only place the text says it went.
That's the one. She "…came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak…" (Luke 8:44) The very next thing Luke says is "immediately her bleeding stopped." Big moment, friend.
Down by His feet is a fair guess, but Luke doesn't say that. The woman "…came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak…" (Luke 8:44) So it's the fringe of His cloak, not a sandal strap.
Nobody points at her in the text. Luke says that after Jesus asks, "…they all denied it." (Luke 8:45) The crowd is just saying it wasn't them. The woman comes forward later, in Luke 8:47.

The text doesn't have anyone blaming anybody. After Jesus asks who touched Him, "…they all denied it." (Luke 8:45) Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, "the people are crowding and pressing against You." Peter sounds like somebody who got asked who bumped them at a packed concert.

That's it. Jesus says, "Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me." (Luke 8:46) That's the reason He gives for knowing. The crowds are pressing around Him, and still He says someone touched Him.

True. Luke says that "In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed." (Luke 8:47) She came trembling, and she still told it with all those people there. I think that took a lot of courage.
The messenger's news is about the girl, not Jairus' wife. He says, "Your daughter is dead…" (Luke 8:49) I think this one hurts, so let's give it room.

Not this crowd. Luke says that when Jesus entered the house, "…He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother." (Luke 8:51) Only those named are allowed to go in with Him. The crowd isn't on that list.

A brother isn't on the list. The text says Jesus allowed in only Peter, John, James, "…and the child’s father and mother." (Luke 8:51) That makes five people allowed to go in with Jesus. The text names no brother for her.

Jesus doesn't give a timeline here. He says, "Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep." (Luke 8:52) No days are mentioned in this passage. Luke says that after Jesus calls to her, "…at once she got up." (Luke 8:54-55)
Yes. Luke says, "And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead." (Luke 8:53) Their laughing comes right after Jesus says she is asleep. Jesus keeps going anyway.

Shouting isn't what the text records. Luke says, "And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead." (Luke 8:53) Their reaction to Jesus is laughing, and the text gives knowing she was dead as the reason.

That's it. Jesus takes her by the hand and calls out, "Child, get up!" (Luke 8:54) Simple words, spoken while holding her hand. Next Luke says, "Her spirit returned, and at once she got up." (Luke 8:55)
I can see why you'd guess that, but it's not what the text says. Jesus took her by the hand and called out, "Child, get up!" (Luke 8:54) The command Luke records is about getting up.
Yes. Luke says Jesus "…directed that she be given something to eat." (Luke 8:55) She has just gotten up, and that's the instruction Jesus gives about her. I think that's about as caring as it gets.

Rest is a natural guess, but the text gives a different instruction. Luke says Jesus "…directed that she be given something to eat." (Luke 8:55) So the instruction is about food. Nothing about rest is mentioned.
